title: Finite local-ring map at a singleton fibre of a finite morphism
statement: Let $p:T\to U$ be a finite morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], let $t\in T$ and $u=p(t)$, and suppose $p^{-1}(\{u\})=\{t\}$. The canonical local-ring homomorphism $p_t^\sharp:\mathcal O_{U,u}\to\mathcal O_{T,t}$ [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is finite, meaning that $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-module. If $p$ is of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], then this ring homomorphism is of finite presentation: for some $a,b\geq0$ there are polynomials $f_1,\ldots,f_b\in\mathcal O_{U,u}[x_1,\ldots,x_a]$ and an $\mathcal O_{U,u}$-algebra isomorphism $\mathcal O_{T,t}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$.

proof.text: Choose an affine open neighbourhood $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $u$ in $U$ and put $W=p^{-1}(V)$. Because $p$ is finite, $W$ is affine, say $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and $A\to B$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ and $\mathfrak q\subset B$ be the primes corresponding to $u$ and $t$ under the affine-point correspondence [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points]. The equality $p^{-1}(\{u\})=\{t\}$ says that $\mathfrak q$ is the unique prime of $B$ contracting to $\mathfrak p$. The affine stalk-localization comparison [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identifies $\mathcal O_{U,u}$ with $A_{\mathfrak p}$, $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ with $B_{\mathfrak q}$. For the affine ring map $\varphi:A\to B$, the definition of the stalk map [def-weil-locally-ringed-space-morphism, def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] gives $p_t^\sharp(a_u)=\varphi(a)_t$. Hence on fractions it sends $a/s$ to $\varphi(a)/\varphi(s)$: the germ identifications therefore identify the actual stalk map with the localized ring map, not just its source and target rings. By [lem-trf-unique-prime-localization], $B_{\mathfrak q}$ is canonically the localization of $B$ at the image of $A\setminus\mathfrak p$, compatibly with this stalk map. The localized map is finite by [lem-trf-localization-finite-ring-map], since finite ring maps remain finite after localization. Transporting across the displayed stalk identifications proves that $p_t^\sharp$ is finite.

proof.text: Assume in addition that $p$ is locally of finite presentation. For the same affine pair $W=\operatorname{Spec}B\to V=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the induced map $A\to B$ is finitely presented by [lem-weil-pbc-lfp-affine-opens-finite-presentation]. Localizing at $A\setminus\mathfrak p$ preserves finite presentation by [lem-trf-localization-finite-presentation-ring-map]. The unique-prime localization isomorphism [lem-trf-unique-prime-localization] and the stalk-localization identifications [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] identify this localized map with $p_t^\sharp$. Hence $p_t^\sharp$ is a finitely presented ring map, which by definition has a presentation $\mathcal O_{T,t}\cong\mathcal O_{U,u}[x_1,\ldots,x_a]/(f_1,\ldots,f_b)$ for suitable $a,b\ge0$ and polynomials $f_i$.
